author: Gino Aalbrecht
title: Source: The Cheesecake Factory corporate website A lot of
text:
Source: The Cheesecake Factory corporate website 
A lot of attention on Seeking Alpha is focused on dividend growth investing. Personally, I do apply the dividend growth investing strategy, and revolve the core of my portfolio around it. A lot of attention on Seeking Alpha is given to dividend aristocrats such as AT&T ( T ), 3M ( MMM ), and McDonald's ( MCD ). These are stocks I own and will keep on owning for a long time. Furthermore, attention goes out to companies that have really stepped up their dividend growth in the last years such as Microsoft ( MSFT ), Boeing ( BA ) and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ). These are all very well known companies and good additions to any dividend growth portfolio.
Today I would like to focus on the dividend growth opportunities of Cheesecake Factory ( CAKE ). Albeit it is a lesser-known company, It is one of the very core holdings of my dividend growth portfolio. In this article, I won’t go into to much detail about the future growth of the entire company. What I would like to say about this is: the company is aiming for 15% shareholder return but is currently missing this target by 1-2% points due to some decline in same-store sales growth. For those interested in an in-depth explanation for the missed target, I’d like to refer to the Q3 Earnings Call Transcript . Furthermore, in the article Cheesecake Factory – A Declining Share Pie I provide more insights on the break down of the 15% target set by management.
